**Sikhae (식해) – A Traditional Korean Fermented Soybean Paste Stew** Sikhae is a hearty, comforting stew that uses *doenjang* (fermented soybean paste) as its base. It’s similar to doenjang jjigae but often includes a richer mix of vegetables, mushrooms, and sometimes seafood or meat. Below is a classic recipe that you can adapt to your taste. --- ### Ingredients *(Serves 4–5 people)* | Item | Amount | Notes | |------|--------|-------| | **Doenjang (fermented soybean paste)** | 3–4 tbsp | Adjust to taste; more gives a stronger flavor. | | **Water or anchovy stock** | 4 cups | Anchovy stock adds depth; use water if you prefer a lighter version. | | **Tofu (firm or silken)** | 1 block (about 300 g) | Cut into bite‑size cubes. | | **Mushrooms** | 1 cup | Shiitake, enoki, or button mushrooms, sliced. | | **Carrot** | 1 medium | Thinly sliced or julienned. | | **Zucchini** | 1 small | Sliced into half‑moon shapes. | | **Onion** | 1 small | Thinly sliced. | | **Garlic** | 2 cloves | Minced. | | **Ginger** | 1 tsp | Grated or minced. | | **Green onions** | 2 stalks | Chopped for garnish. | | **Korean chili flakes (gochugaru)** | 1 tsp | Optional, for a mild kick. | | **Sesame oil** | 1 tsp | For finishing. | | **Salt & pepper** | to taste | Adjust after tasting. | | **Optional additions** | | • Kimchi (small pieces)
• Seafood (shrimp, clams)
• Beef or pork slices
• Spinach or kale | --- ### Equipment - Medium‑sized pot or Dutch oven - Cutting board & knife - Measuring spoons --- ### Instructions 1. **Prepare the Stock** - If using anchovy stock: simmer 4 cups of water with a handful of dried anchovies, a piece of kombu (seaweed), and a pinch of salt for about 10 minutes. Strain and discard solids. - If using plain water, just bring it to a boil. 2. **Add the Doenjang** - Reduce heat to medium. Add the doenjang to the stock and stir until fully dissolved. - Let it simmer for 2–3 minutes so the flavors meld. 3. **Add Aromatics** - Stir in minced garlic, grated ginger, and optional gochugaru. - Simmer for another minute. 4. **Add Vegetables** - Add carrots, zucchini, onion, and mushrooms. - Cover and let the stew simmer for about 5–7 minutes, or until the vegetables are tender but still crisp. 5. **Add Tofu & Optional Ingredients** - Gently fold in tofu cubes. - If you’re adding kimchi, seafood, or meat, add them now. - Simmer for an additional 3–5 minutes. - Taste and season with salt and pepper as needed. 6. **Finish** - Drizzle sesame oil over the stew. - Sprinkle chopped green onions on top. 7. **Serve** - Ladle the stew into bowls. - Serve hot with steamed rice and side dishes (banchan). - A splash of fresh lime juice or a drizzle of chili oil can add a bright finish if desired. --- ### Tips & Variations - **Texture**: Silken tofu gives a silky mouthfeel, while firm tofu holds its shape better. - **Flavor Depth**: Adding a splash of soy sauce or a few drops of fish sauce can deepen the umami. - **Heat Level**: Increase gochugaru or add fresh sliced red chilies for more spice. - **Vegetable Mix**: Feel free to swap in other root veggies (daikon, sweet potato) or leafy greens (spinach, bok choy). - **Leftovers**: Sikhae keeps well in the fridge for 1–2 days. Reheat gently on low heat to avoid breaking the tofu. Enjoy your homemade sikhae! It’s a perfect comfort food for chilly evenings or when you need a quick, nourishing meal.
